positions.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Wed 9/16 at the close, ahead of the FOMC statement, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 PHYSICAL SUPPLY SHOCK. Saudi Arabia shut its ~750-mile East-West (Petroline) pipeline over the weekend after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq. That pipeline is the kingdom's only route for moving crude to Red Sea export terminals WITHOUT transiting the Strait of Hormuz, so its loss removes the alternative at the exact moment the strait itself has become dangerous: a merchant vessel was struck inside Hormuz killing one crew member, and transit traffic fell to single digits per day over the weekend against a 10-day average of 14 and a pre-war norm near 125. Reuters sources say Saudi export stocks could run out within five to seven days. Brent for November is +3.4% to $108.17 and WTI October +3% to $103.07, on top of a 20%+ move over the past month. Marathon is the largest US independent refiner at ~3.0M bpd of capacity and the cleanest expression of the trade, because the disruption is to internationally traded CRUDE while Marathon's Gulf Coast system runs largely domestic and Canadian barrels and sells product into a globally short market - the crack widens rather than compresses. MPC is bid +1.85% pre-market to 403.24 from the 9/11 close of 395.93, the strongest confirming move in the refining group and ahead of XLE at +1.24%. Friday's session was itself a breakout: opened 395.31, ran to 409.11 and printed a new 52-week high on 2.36M shares against a 2.39M 30-day average.
positions.risks: This is a headline-driven position and the headline can reverse in one sentence: a confirmed Petroline restart or credible de-escalation out of the postponed Oman talks would unwind the entire move, which is why this is sized to a 5% stop rather than held to a target. The stock made its 52-week high on Friday, so there is no overhead supply to absorb a reversal and nothing above to lean on - I am buying an extended chart. Refiner margins are a spread, not a price: if crude rises faster than products the crack compresses and the thesis inverts. The FOMC meets Wednesday and Thursday with roughly 86% priced for a 25bp HIKE, and this same oil impulse is what is driving that pricing - a hawkish dot plot hits the market broadly even as it validates the energy trade. Pre-market pricing carries wider spreads than the 403.50/404.64 quote suggests once size is involved.
positions.driver: Saudi Petroline shutdown plus a Hormuz vessel strike with transit down to single digits a day, lifting Brent 3.4% to $108.17, taken through the largest US independent refiner at +1.85% pre-market.

positions.name: Valero Energy Corporation
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Wed 9/16 at the close, ahead of the FOMC statement, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 PHYSICAL SUPPLY SHOCK - same named catalyst as MPC, expressed through the most export-weighted US refiner. Valero runs 15 refineries and is the largest US exporter of refined product, which matters specifically here: the Petroline shutdown and the collapse in Hormuz transit (single digits per day versus a pre-war 125) disrupt seaborne crude supply to Europe and Asia, and the marginal replacement barrel of gasoline and diesel for those markets comes off the US Gulf Coast. Valero is bid +1.61% pre-market to 396.71 from the 9/11 close of 390.42. Friday's session printed a new 52-week high of 399.255 on 3.06M shares against a 2.44M 30-day average - 1.25x relative volume, so the breakout had real participation behind it rather than being a quiet drift. At 16.2x earnings and a 4.5x book the valuation is undemanding relative to the move.
positions.risks: Same reversal risk as MPC and it is the dominant one: this is a two-name expression of a single geopolitical headline, so MPC and VLO will move together and a Petroline restart takes both down at once. Also at a 52-week high with no support beneath. Valero carries more renewable-diesel and ethanol exposure than Marathon, segments that have been a persistent drag and that do not benefit from a crude supply shock. Crack-spread inversion risk if crude outruns products. The FOMC decision lands Thursday with a hike roughly 86% priced - this position is closed Wednesday specifically to avoid holding through it.
positions.driver: Second leg of the Hormuz/Petroline refining trade through the largest US product exporter, +1.61% pre-market after a 1.25x-volume 52-week-high breakout on Friday.

positions.name: Occidental Petroleum Corporation
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on a confirmed Petroline restart or a credible Hormuz de-escalation headline, by Wed 9/16 at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 PHYSICAL SUPPLY SHOCK, taken through the highest crude beta in the book. Occidental is the most oil-levered US large cap in this group - upstream-weighted with a balance sheet still carrying CrownRock acquisition debt, which means realized-price moves flow to equity with leverage in both directions. With Brent +3.4% to $108.17 and WTI +3% to $103.07, and Reuters sources indicating Saudi export stocks could be exhausted within five to seven days, this is the position that pays most if the disruption persists past this week. OXY is bid +1.72% pre-market to 62.52 from the 9/11 close of 61.46, the strongest confirming move among the large-cap producers and ahead of XOM (+1.48%) and COP (+1.54%), with a tight 62.52/62.68 quote. The stock is 7.3% below its 67.45 52-week high from March and 61% above its December low of 38.80, so there is room above rather than a breakout to chase.
positions.risks: The leverage cuts both ways and harder than it does at Exxon: the same balance sheet that amplifies a crude rally amplifies the unwind if Petroline restarts, which is why this is catalyst-defined with a 5% stop rather than held to a date. The catalyst here is explicitly a NEWS state, not a price level - if the Oman de-escalation talks are rescheduled and produce anything, this position exits the same session regardless of P&L. OXY went ex-dividend 9/10 so there is no distribution inside the window. Occidental's chemical segment (OxyChem) sees input costs rise with crude, a partial internal offset. The FOMC hike roughly 86% priced for Thursday is a broad-market headwind and the reason the position cannot be held past Wednesday.
positions.driver: Highest crude beta among US large-cap producers with the strongest confirming pre-market move in the group (+1.72%), held against a named news trigger rather than a date.

positions.name: Frontline plc
positions.exitRule: Catalyst-defined - flat on Hormuz transit normalising back toward its pre-war ~125 vessels/day or a confirmed Petroline restart, by Wed 9/16 at the latest, or on a 5% stop
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 - this is the purest claim on the specific disruption rather than on the oil price. Frontline is the largest listed VLCC owner, and tanker equities are levered to FREIGHT RATES, which are set by ton-mile demand and by risk premium, not by the price of the barrel. Both inputs just moved hard in the same direction: Hormuz transit collapsed to single digits per day over the weekend against a 10-day average of 14 and a pre-war norm near 125, one merchant vessel was struck inside the strait killing a crew member, and the Petroline shutdown means Saudi barrels that would have exited via the Red Sea must now either wait or go through the strait - lengthening voyages and shrinking effective fleet supply at the same time war-risk insurance premiums reprice. FRO is bid +1.91% pre-market to 50.15 from the 9/11 close of 49.21, tight two-sided at 50.10/50.19. Friday printed a new 52-week high of 49.56 on 3.71M shares against a 2.52M 30-day average - 1.47x relative volume, the strongest volume confirmation of any name entered today. The stock trades at 7.4x earnings.
positions.risks: Tanker equities are the most violent mean-reverters in the market: the same mechanism that adds 2% on a transit disruption removes 10% on a de-escalation headline, and this name already ran through last week, so I am entering an extended move at a 52-week high with nothing beneath it. A ceasefire or convoy arrangement ends this trade instantly, which is why the exit is defined against a transit-normalisation headline rather than a date. Frontline is Cyprus-domiciled with 85 employees and a $11.0B market cap - it is a rate vehicle, not an operating business, and it carries no earnings floor if rates roll. FRO goes ex-dividend 9/18 at $2.61 (a 6.4% yield), which is AFTER this position's latest exit date, so the distribution is not captured and a pre-ex-date run-up is a possible tailwind rather than something I am relying on.
positions.driver: Purest listed claim on the Hormuz transit collapse via VLCC freight rates rather than the crude price, +1.91% pre-market after a 1.47x-volume 52-week-high breakout.

positions.name: DHT Holdings, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Wed 9/16 at the close, ahead of the FOMC statement, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 - second VLCC vehicle on the Hormuz ton-mile shock, and the strongest confirming pre-market move of any name entered today at +2.09%, to 22.46 from the 9/11 close of 22.00, on a tight 22.33/22.45 quote. DHT is a pure crude-tanker owner with no refining, chemical or upstream segments to dilute the rate exposure, which makes it a cleaner read on spot VLCC economics than the diversified names. The mechanism is the same as Frontline's and is specific: with Hormuz traffic at single digits a day versus a pre-war 125, and the Petroline bypass shut after drone attacks, effective fleet supply contracts while voyage lengths extend. Friday's session printed a new 52-week high of 22.28 on 5.21M shares against a 3.48M 30-day average - 1.50x relative volume. DHT trades at 7.5x earnings with an 11.1% trailing dividend yield, so the equity is priced as though current rates are a peak that will not persist.
positions.risks: Everything said about Frontline applies here with more force: DHT is a $3.5B market cap, the smallest name in this book, and it will move 2-3x the index in either direction. It is also the second position on an identical mechanism, so FRO and DHT are effectively one doubled bet on Hormuz rather than two ideas - a de-escalation headline hits both simultaneously and the sector cap of two names is what keeps that exposure bounded. Entering at a 52-week high after the move has already run. The 11.1% yield reflects the market's view that spot rates mean-revert, not a sustainable distribution. DHT went ex-dividend 8/17 so there is nothing to capture inside the window. Closed Wednesday specifically to avoid the Thursday FOMC statement.
positions.driver: Strongest confirming pre-market move on the board (+2.09%) in the purest crude-tanker vehicle, on 1.50x-volume 52-week-high confirmation Friday.

positions.name: Cheniere Energy, Inc.
positions.exitRule: 1-3 day swing - exit Wed 9/16 at the close, ahead of the FOMC statement, or on a 5% stop / 8% take-profit
positions.catalyst: Tier 1 SUBSTITUTION TRADE on the same shock, through a different commodity. Cheniere is the largest US LNG exporter, operating Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi. When Gulf hydrocarbon supply becomes unreliable - Petroline shut, Hormuz transit down to single digits a day, Saudi export stocks possibly exhausted within five to seven days - European and Asian buyers bid up the substitute they can physically receive, which is US seaborne LNG, and Qatari LNG itself must transit Hormuz, making the disruption directly bullish for Atlantic-basin supply. LNG is bid +1.24% pre-market to 281.80 from the 9/11 close of 278.34. Unlike the refiners and tankers this name is NOT extended: at 281.80 it sits 6.3% below its 300.89 52-week high from March, so the entry is into a name that has not yet been marked for this catalyst rather than one already at a high.
positions.risks: Cheniere's economics are overwhelmingly fixed-fee, take-or-pay contracted, which is the point of the business model and the problem with the trade: near-term spot LNG strength flows to the P&L far less than a headline would imply, so this is a sentiment repricing rather than an earnings event. That also explains the more modest +1.24% confirmation - the tape agrees it is a weaker linkage than the tanker names. At 9.3x book it is the most expensive asset base in this group. A Petroline restart or Hormuz normalisation removes the premium. Friday's volume of 1.48M was well below the 1.89M 30-day average, so participation into the entry is thin. LNG went ex-dividend 8/10; nothing inside the window. Closed Wednesday ahead of the FOMC statement.
positions.driver: US LNG as the physical substitute for disrupted Gulf supply, entered 6.3% below its March 52-week high rather than at a breakout like the rest of the energy book.
